# Compatibility gap map (Unity 6000.0.71f1)

What Unbound does not yet do as the Editor does, found by auditing the engine itself rather than
waiting for a game to hit it. `ROADMAP.md` says what is done and probed; this file lists what is
left, ranked, so work can go down it.

Audit of 2026-10-29: read-only, every subsystem; nothing was measured against the Editor, so each
row still needs a probe before and after it is fixed. Paths are relative to `managed/UnityEngine/`
unless they start with `crates/` or `native/`.

## API declaration follow-ups

AssetBundleManifest typed reader and independent clone ownership are covered by
`tests/projects/manifestadapters` on Unity 6000.0.71f1, with 913 exact controls across
three bundle formats, array mutation and unload/reload. Other declaration debt stays
in [API_DECLARATION_FOLLOWUPS.md](API_DECLARATION_FOLLOWUPS.md).

## Known insignificant residuals

By the user's decision of 2026-11-01, small differences with no visible effect or
game-logic change do not block package admission. Raw values and comparator
tolerances stay unchanged; strict verifiers still report these failures.
Roughly 1-3/255 in isolated pixels is an example, not a blanket tolerance.
Visible or functional systematic biases, wrong functional answers, changes in
survival, death/event timing or ordering, and actual bugs remain actionable.
A numeric lifetime-field difference alone does not establish a functional change;
its effect on the measured histories still matters. No Native captures or deep research are spent solely
to eliminate a listed insignificant residual.

No effect on the root's path (rootPosition, deltaPosition match). Measured 2026-11-06 (Unbound traced against the reference): (1) velocity: the deltaPosition errors are about one float step of the clip-space root motion (values about 1, 1.2e-7) times the root's scale 100 and humanScale 1.05, about 1.25e-5 world, of either sign and without bias (whole steps on the large forward z component, fractions of one on x and y); velocity multiplies them by 30, and whichever component is small beside the others fails the relative check (y about 0.9 beside z about 40, or z on `blendTransition.step24`, `settingsFeetRight.step11` and `stateMirrorB`). (2) pivot: at `blendTransition.step18` both feet slips are 1.4e-7 and 1.6e-7 (clip units, a few float steps of the foot positions), so their ratio is rounding; at `settingsBakeOffset.step15`/`settingsCycle.step23` pivotWeight differs by 7.7e-6/1.6e-5 (within tolerance) and the feet are about 60 world units apart, giving 4e-4 on pivotPosition[0]. (3) arm twist: `HumanPoseHandler.GetHumanPose` removes the forearm's y rotation by turning the upper arm, stopping at the first iteration whose angle grows (under 1 degree). For these IK poses the angle does not converge: it stays at 0.6496 degrees, moving by float noise (about 1e-5 degrees) each iteration, while each iteration moves one 0.0036 step of twist from the forearm to the upper arm. Forcing 1 to 5 iterations reproduces Unity's value at every one of the 116 steps; which count Unity stops at depends on the last bits. In the Editor too, nearly the same looped pose (`ik.step3` and `step27`, `ikB.step0`/`26`, `3`/`27`, `6`/`28`, the other 93 muscles within 1.5e-5) reads back one to three steps apart. No visible effect in the probe (the transforms match; the two muscles' sum matches); a game that writes the read pose back with SetHumanPose gets the twist split between upper arm and forearm differently by up to that much, as the Editor's own spread does. No systematic cause: recorded, not fixed. Since Humanoid transform keys take the single-precision frame times (2026-11-11) the same three families sit on partly other keys: velocity also on `crossFade`, `exit020`, `mixer.clipB`, `mixer.weight1`, `settingsBakeOrig`, `settingsOrigRot` and `stateMirrorB` steps, pivotPosition[0] on `eventsMirrorCycle.step8`, `stateMirrorCycle` and `transitionMirror` in place of `settingsBakeOffset.step15`, the arm twist on other `ik*` steps; five leg-muscle values of the Foot IK family newly exceed the tolerance (`stream.ik.step10` and `stream.ikPass.step10` muscles[35] by 2.4e-3 and muscles[33] by 8.1e-4, `stream.bodyLocal.step24` muscles[31] by 3.4e-4: the sizes the family has on its other steps) while eight listed ones match; they count as differences, the list in `known.json` only shrinks. Foot IK legs: up to 2.4e-3 on one step. Read-back solve: arm roll muscles up to 9e-3 (their sum within 9e-5), left foot muscles up to 1.4e-3; the class is bounded, not listed: each of these muscles and the two local rotations within 1e-2, the roll muscles' sum within 1e-4 on every step | Measured 2026-11-11, one rig and one clip, with every transform recorded in Editor captures outside the reference. (1) Stance (a job resets the stream to the stance pose each update, the state's Foot IK then pulls the straight legs to a walk's foot goals, root motion applied): the Editor's values depend on how far the Animator is from the origin (here root motion moves it; Q548 below: a static placement does the same); Unbound's muscles do not, and its stream body about seven times less. Kept at the origin (`stream.stanceInPlace`, in the reference) the two agree on every value. With root motion the muscles the Editor's job reads right after the reset already step as the root moves (the left upper leg's front-back 0.5996863 to 0.5996884 in updates 0 to 3, 0.5997035 in update 4, 0.5996372 in 5 to 7 and 0.5997034 from 8; 0.5996863 on every update in place, 0.5996861 in Unbound), its stream body after the reset wanders over 2.5e-4 where it is constant in place (Unbound's over 3.4e-5), and in the final pose the hips' local position is off Unbound's by about (0, 1.3e-6, -0.5e-6) of the root's local units in updates 5 to 7, about (0, 6e-6, 1.5e-6) in 13 to 20 and (0, -3.5e-5, -5.9e-6) from 21 on (times 100 in the world; under 5e-7 in the other updates), the arms' rotations by up to 0.038 degrees and the legs' by up to 0.047; the hips and the arms sit on runs of updates with steps between them, the legs change every update from 21 on. Every step starts at the update where the root's world z first passes a power of two: 2 at update 4, 4 at 5, 8 at 8, 16 at 13 and 32 at 21; each step so far is larger than the last, and the root is 46 world units from the origin by update 28. Unbound's hips follow a smooth, symmetric path over the cycle. That is the mark of single-precision loss in the reset away from the origin rather than of a missing Foot IK mechanism; what exactly produces the steps is not known (Q548 below locates it in the reset's body). Q548 (Linux GPU Editor captures outside the reference, root motion off, the stance job and HumanA's clip without it on an Animator placed at z 0, 3, 40, 1000, 1e5 and 2.8e6): the drift needs no root motion, only the distance: the stance job matches the Editor at 0 and 3 and differs from 40 on (muscles up to 5.4e-3 and the body up to 3.3e-3 at 40, 4.2e-3 and 2.7e-3 at 1000, the body's z by 23 at 2.8e6), while the clip without the job, Foot IK included, matches at every offset (pose within 1e-4). It starts in what the stream answers right after `ResetToStancePose`: of the five muscles the job reads there, the Editor's move with the offset from z 3 on (the left upper leg's front-back 0.5996863 at 0, 0.5997035 at 3 and 40, 0.59970367 at 1000; the right arm's down-up by up to 4e-5) while Unbound's stay as at the origin, and the body carries most of the difference: both engines' stance body comes out on the float grid of the world offset (steps of 6.1e-5 at 1000, 0.0078 at 1e5; y alike), its z 405 steps in the Editor and 393 in Unbound at 1000 (the exact stance 390.3), 4 and 5 steps at 1e5, and at 2.8e6 (steps of 0.25) -96 steps (-24) in the Editor against 2 (0.5) in Unbound (the exact stance 0.024, 0.1 step); the Editor's x moves by up to 6e-6 with the offset where Unbound's does not. Unbound's error stays within about three steps of the grid; the Editor's does not (15 steps at 1000, about 96 at 2.8e6): a coarser computation through world-sized values, whose operations these captures do not identify. Only a job that resets the stream to the stance away from the origin was measured to trigger it. Also ruled out: rounding of the foot goals (moving them by one single-precision step changes Unbound's result by at most 3e-7 on the body and 1e-4 on a muscle; measured once, runs not kept), the stabilize-feet path (off here), the pivot weight (equal within 6e-6, no event at those updates). (2) Foot IK legs after a job changed the pose: moving the foot goals by one single-precision step changes Unbound's own result by the same 2.4e-3 on the same value (`stream.ik.step10` muscles[35]) and by no more than 6e-6 when the job only reads; the difference is consistent with amplified rounding of a nearly straight leg (measured once, runs not kept). Since Humanoid transform keys take the single-precision frame times the family sits on other steps (five values counted as differences, one left in `known.json`; `stream.bodyLocal` step 17 muscles 23 and 25, up to 5.7e-4, joined it with the Mono float opt-in, where game code's quaternion products evaluate as Mono does). (3) A solve after the job read the pose back on the root scaled by 100 (`bone.rotateThenSolve`, `bone.solveTwice`, 140 keys in `known.json` from Unbound runs on macOS and Linux; with the Mono float opt-in, game code's quaternion products evaluated as Mono does move the split onto other steps, `readback-solve-straight-limbs`, recorded with the macOS Editor): the goal is out of reach of the re-based skeleton in both (the body displaced toward the root alike) and the left arm straight; the upper arm and forearm roll muscles split one roll between them, and Unbound's split is off the Editor's in steps of 1.8e-3 (up to 9e-3) that cancel in their sum within 9e-5, with the upper arm's and hand's local rotations following; moving the goal by one single-precision step moves Unbound's own split by 5.4e-3 (step 16, measured once, runs not kept): amplified rounding of a straight arm. The left foot's muscles 26 and 27 are off by up to 1.4e-3 on five steps of each control, not traced further. |

## Failing probes by cause (triage of 2026-11-11)

Every probe that failed in the sheriff's full suite on `a6f0d8af2` (148 pass / 45 fail / 10 report
of 203) and had no open task, with what its failures are and where they are recorded. Counts are
that run's, except for the named follow-up replays in each row, including
Q369/Q296/Q363/Q248 and Q372/Q368/Q353. One probe can hold several causes; each is listed with its own count. Classes:

- **order**: an order or text Unity's documentation leaves open (see the notes under the table);
- **residual**: listed in [Known insignificant residuals](#known-insignificant-residuals);
- **gap**: a real difference, with the row of the map that carries it;
- **probe**: a defect of the probe, its recipe or the way its reference was recorded.

Corrected references are identified below. Comparators and tolerances are unchanged, and raw
engine differences still fail. The shared sheriff baseline has not been promoted by this work.

The 2026-11-12 lifecycle and scripting follow-ups close inherited Edit-mode execution and startup ownership
(`editinheritance`, 171/171 values), imported texture flags (`assetclones`, 14340/14340),
Editor/Play exit controls (`editorcallbacks`, 114/114 values across four quit profiles),
internal reflection/particle-light root ownership (`hiddenroots`, 15/15),
public flag transitions (`hiddenflags`, 557/557), and material reload identity
(`droppedparams`, 252/252; `materialalias`, 62/62), and captured exception output
(`stackcapture`, 15/15; `testrunner`, all 11 PlayMode nodes).
CRT scheduling now matches all 448 customrt values and 228 images, with 229
additional load-cycle controls in crtload. Created-clip memory matches 81 controls
and closes five appfacts values.
The retained callback order, queued-load timing, stack-utility text, input,
importer and numerical differences below remain visible in the strict comparisons.
Each gap row gives the measured context and the remaining follow-up scope.
The implementation follow-ups are shared serialized engine-property bindings,
general game float evaluation, and the remaining memory and stack-utility coverage. Exact async
completion frames and cross-object callback order retain their scoped records.

### Order and text Unity's documentation leaves open

- **Order between GameObjects.** Manual 6000.0, *Order of execution for event functions*,
  Limitations: "In general, you can't rely on the order in which the same event function is invoked
  for different GameObjects, except when the order is explicitly documented or settable", and the
  `Update` of one MonoBehaviour "might be called before or after the Update function for the same
  MonoBehaviour on another GameObject, including its own parent or child GameObjects". The
  activationorder keys, the 24 editorcallbacks events and 59 oroorder lines are such orders
  (`OnRenderObject`'s page says only that it "is called after camera has rendered the Scene", on
  "any object that has a script with the function"). In each of them the two sides hold the same
  events with the same payloads; each object's own Awake, OnEnable, Start sequence and the
  configurable script execution order are kept. What is not shown: that no game depends on the
  Editor's order. A game that does would behave differently, as it could between two Editor
  releases; the raw sequences stay in the reports.
- **Exception message text.** The exceptions are of the documented type. Game code reads an
  argument exception's parameter name on a second line (`Parameter name: name`) as in the Editor
  (row "Argument exception texts"); one `NullReferenceException` message the runtime raises ends
  with a full stop only in Unbound. No Unity page documents the text. A game that parses it would
  see the difference.
- **When the render thread has run a plugin's callbacks (multithreaded rendering).** With
  `-force-gfx-mt` on Vulkan, Unity 6000.0's Scripting API says only that the native pointer getters
  (`Texture.GetNativeTexturePtr`, `RenderTexture.GetNativeDepthBufferPtr`,
  `GraphicsBuffer`/`ComputeBuffer.GetNativeBufferPtr`, `Mesh.GetNativeVertexBufferPtr`/`GetNativeIndexBufferPtr`; Unbound
  does not implement the Mesh ones) synchronize with the rendering thread; Unbound waits at the
  others and at readbacks. In every Editor capture of tests/projects/nativegfx recorded before the
  probe waited for the render thread itself (`run.py --mt` captures of 2026-11-22), the callbacks
  issued before `Camera.Render`, `Graphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer`, a render texture's creation and
  clear, or the end of a frame had run by the probe's next change of plugin state; Unbound's can run
  them later (a frame-1 callback ran after frame 2's script set the plugin's next step). Which Editor
  call waits is unmeasured and undocumented. A plugin that sets state from a script and reads it in
  a callback issued earlier, without its own synchronization, sees the difference. The probe now
  waits before it changes such state, so its comparison no longer shows it.

### Probe and reference repairs

- **Recording mode, Q363.** `destroycontract`, `activationorder` and `shaderpasscount`
  now use two identical windowed GPU Editor captures from the existing display. The
  [Unity 6000.0 EOF limitation](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/ScriptReference/WaitForEndOfFrame.html)
  excludes batch-mode execution. Their READMEs state every changed row scope.
  Destroycontract still fails 887 keys because first-render/EOF startup differs in
  this fixture; re-recording did not establish engine parity.
- **Numeric recorder, Q363.** Oroorder now names only explicitly formatted instance
  IDs. Two Editor repeats preserve every reference line. Its 23 corrupted numeric
  payload pairs are resolved; the other 91 missing/extra pairs remain raw.
- **TextCore recipe and counter, Q369.** The font recipe already copies and verifies
  both fonts, so all 372 cases run. The suite now reads `N of M values differ` and
  counts the existing 8226 failures. S19 stored zero counted failures because its
  parser missed that form, and its missing-font recipe compared no cases. A replay
  against that unchanged baseline therefore flags the visibility increase. It is
  not waived and no baseline is promoted here.
- **Wind clock, Q363.** A fixed capture interval replaces wall-time-dependent
  phases. All 18 records match, with the same raw comparator and tolerances.
- **Work-area sampling, Q296.** Inputplatform waits up to ten seconds for both
  changed and restored work areas. A 30-frame delayed control passes 11/11; the
  ten-frame sampler fails that control at `workArea.changed`. The normal control
  passes 43/43 and the undelayed work-area control 11/11. All five Editor reference
  files remain byte-identical.
- **Stopwatch units, Q248.** The new Linux Editor reference has 12 records from two
  identical windowed GPU captures, including an escaping readonly field reference.
  The original runtime matches 6/12, the corrected one 12/12. Engine-internal timer
  units are unchanged; the game-assembly members use the measured 100 ns unit.

## How gaps hide

Game runs keep hitting features that are missing *without a warning* (physical cameras,
`Camera.SetReplacementShader`). The generated stubs warn on first use; these do not:

| Pattern | Example | Why it is silent |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-written empty body | `Camera.SetReplacementShader { }`, `Animator.ApplyBuiltinRootMotion` | A hand-written member suppresses the generated stub, and with it the warning (516 empty public bodies in the hand-written sources, many legitimate) |
| Stored, never consumed | `Physics2D.simulationLayers` | Auto-properties and fields the frame/simulation never reads |
| Serialized field or import setting not read | `m_DisabledShaderPasses`, `m_RenderingPath`, terrain lightmap, ModelImporter clip masks/root motion, `m_ContactPairsMode` | `ReadSerialized` / the importers read a subset of keys and drop the rest |
| Message looked up, never sent | done: `Messages.cs` `s_NotSent` (empty since OnParticleUpdateJobScheduled is sent) warns once per script class for a listed message | Messages are not API calls: `api-gaps` cannot see them |
| Overload drops a parameter | `Graphics.ConvertTexture(src, srcElement, dst, dstElement)`, `Mesh.Set*(..., flags)`, stereo-eye overloads (Blit slices, `LogOption`, `SetPropertyBlock` index done) | Forwarded to the simpler overload |
| Asset class with a ClassId but no reader | done (`classids`): a class without a reader warns once at load, naming the class and the file, and `unbound doctor` lists the project's files holding one | Ignored classes (`ClassCoverage.s_Ignored`, with a reason) stay silent |
| Stub default not neutral | done (`stubdefaults`): value-returning stubs take the Editor's answer from `StubDefaults.cs` where it is a constant; `ScalableBufferManager` and `CalculateObliqueMatrix` are hand-written, `Microphone.devices` takes the generator's empty-array rule | Members whose answer is not a constant still return the default after their warning (see the tooling item) |
| Generated stub events | done: subscribing warns that the event is never raised | |
| Claimed capability | done for the measured NVIDIA OpenGL Core and Vulkan `SystemInfo.supportsTextureWrapMirrorOnce` cases: native mirror-clamp is used where supported | Other driver capability profiles remain unmeasured |
| Warn once, then silent | SpriteMask, reflection probes | A second scene shows nothing in the log |

callbacks, FormerlySerializedAs), prefab variants/nesting/overrides, Time, PlayerPrefs.

Documented (Scripting API 6000.0): Application.backgroundLoadingPriority limits the main-thread integration time of asynchronous operations per frame (Low 2, BelowNormal 4, Normal 10, High 50 ms; default BelowNormal; the page says the setting has no effect in the Editor); AsyncOperation.priority orders queued operations that have not started; allowSceneActivation holds at 0.9 and stalls the queue; EditorSettings.forceAssetUnloadAndGCOnSceneLoad unloads unused assets and collects the managed heap after a Single load. The probe records absolute frames only beyond the limit and checks every other gap against the pass time it measured. Resources.LoadAsync, AssetBundle.LoadFromFileAsync and AssetBundle.LoadAssetAsync (and, inferred, the other AssetBundle create and asset-load requests) wait in the same queue behind requests made before them (a held scene load holds them; tests/projects/sceneunload `queue.*`) and complete when they reach its head; with nothing queued they complete at the next preloading pass as before. `--queue-only` matches because Unbound's first integration of a session takes about 7 ms (first-use compilation); a faster first integration would make it a raw failure under the same rule. Unmeasured: the order when the loader took a request before its priority was set (it varies between Editor runs; a sidecar diagnostic), the macOS read-back and a Linux user allowed to raise thread priorities, other asynchronous operations (AssetBundle.UnloadAsync, NavMesh builds) in the queue, other releases (previous one-pass timing) |

Texture2D: a side of zero or less is refused (an assertion first for a negative side), the constructor throws and Reinitialize answers false; pixel arrays and blocks name the API and the texture; GetPixel/SetPixel/GetPixelBilinear log an undefined mip; GetPixelData names the valid mip range; a Graphics.CopyTexture region outside the source or destination level logs its error and copies nothing, a whole copy between 2D textures of other sizes logs the size mismatch and copies nothing, while an element or mip copy between them copies the source level's bytes in order to its CPU pixels when both levels hold as many bytes (levels of other sizes measured; of other formats inferred; the GPU copy takes the region both share, the Editor's GPU side being unmeasured); between uncompressed formats with other byte counts it logs the data size mismatch (the GraphicsFormat numbers and byte counts) and copies nothing (compressed levels of other sizes copy, tests/projects/texturecompression `copy.mip`; an uncompressed with a compressed level is unmeasured and not checked). Every copy naming a source or destination element or level that does not exist logs it and copies nothing; a region with a negative width or height logs it and copies nothing (engine stand-ins for procedural draws keep whole triangles only). Cubemap, Texture2DArray, Texture3D, CubemapArray: GetPixels, SetPixels and SetPixels32 name the API and the texture for a face, element or level that does not exist; SetPixels of a layered texture refuses no array as not a valid argument and a short one as too little data and writes from the start of a longer one, SetPixels32 refuses a longer one as outside the level; Cubemap.SetPixels refuses no or a short array as too little data; GetPixel and SetPixel log an undefined face or level (Texture3D.GetPixel calls an undefined level an image) and answer white or do nothing; GetPixelData names the valid level, face or element range as the release's managed code does; SetPixelData refuses a face or element as not a valid argument, then the level, then too little data (Cubemap.SetPixelData is implemented, its bytes read back through GetPixel/GetPixels and its blocks for a compressed cube). Animator and AnimatorControllerPlayable: lookups warn (a bad layer is a warning), without a controller each lookup warns and Play/CrossFade name the missing controller; a parameter given by id is named 'Hash id', a type mismatch names the parameter as called; a state missing on any layer also reports layer -1; a controller playable no output plays answers from its controller's state (a detached player that is never stepped and makes no behaviours): its warnings are measured, its other answers (parameter count and values, layer weights, the start state's info) are Unbound's (unmeasured), and so is the hand-over: the player of the Animator an output then plays it on starts with the parameter values, layer weights and pending Play/CrossFade requests set on it; `logWarnings` silences only the parameter and controller warnings; GetLayerName answers "" and a bare GetLayerWeight -1. Exceptions stay the class library's (exact class, ParamName, ActualValue: catch clauses, exact type tests and test frameworks' Assert.Throws see the Editor's classes), and game code reads Mono's texts whoever threw the exception: its virtual reads of Exception.Message and the calls that make an exception text (a virtual ToString, string.Concat and string.Format, StringBuilder.Append and AppendFormat, Convert.ToString) are redirected when its assemblies load and in hot-reload deltas, with Mono's number formatting (the class library's tuples' items too, also in a value tuple's own ToString(); an edit made by hot reload goes through the shims an assembly that formats anything already references, except a ToString called directly on a value tuple, an enum or a generic parameter's value, which an edit writes as .NET does); Debug.LogException, an uncaught exception's log line, "Rethrow as" lines and Debug.Log of an exception write Mono's texts. ### Built-in render pipeline

Done: forward base/add lighting, vertex/SH lights, shadows (cascades, spot, point; casters from
fallback shaders), camera matrices and physical cameras, clear flags, MSAA, command buffers at
every forward event, OnPre*/OnPost*/OnRenderImage and [ImageEffectOpaque], depth, depth-normals
and motion-vector textures, sorting layers, SortingGroup and transparency sort axes, fog, ambient
modes, lightmaps and light probes, custom, baked and realtime reflection probes with blending/box
projection, keywords, GrabPass, LODGroup, SubShader LOD, disabled passes, `.renderTexture`
assets, Display 1 only, projectors, replacement shaders, oblique mirrors with inverted culling,
cubemap renders, camera skyboxes, deferred and vertex-lit paths, material variants, raster
states (tests/projects/builtinrp, builtinfx, display, baked, lighting).

In those samples a quadrant of the 9x9 target, with a corner at its centre, held transparent zeros or another image. The window present on Bevy's render thread now waits for its copy before it releases the OpenGL context that the game thread also renders with (vendor/wgpu-sampler/PATCHES.md `gl-present-wait.patch`). With this wait the wrong samples are gone (measured: 0 in 6 runs). Inferred, not measured: the present overlaps the game thread's rendering on the shared context. This is measured on the NVIDIA 580 driver only. Which driver operation overlaps is not known. Other drivers are unmeasured. No wrong sample was seen in 4 runs on the Vulkan device. `LOD_PROBE_REPEAT` repeats each sample's render to look for this under load (README). A camera draws the first level from `QualitySettings.maximumLODLevel` on whose reach, the group's world size over the level's transition height, is more than the camera's distance to the reference point times 2 tan(fov / 2) / `lodBias` (orthographic: twice the size over the bias, at any distance); at equality the next level is drawn. Documented: the transition height is screen-relative in [0, 1] and `lodBias` multiplies the switching distance (Scripting API 6000.0 [LOD.screenRelativeTransitionHeight](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/ScriptReference/LOD-screenRelativeTransitionHeight.html), [QualitySettings.lodBias](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/ScriptReference/QualitySettings-lodBias.html)); the tie rule is measured. Unbound's choices, not measured: a group of size 0 and a level of height 0, or `lodBias` 0 with the camera at the reference point, draw nothing. Not modelled (measured on one machine only, probe `run.py editor --hold`, not in the reference): in the Editor a camera rendered again within about 1 ms of real time can draw the levels chosen for its previous place (a 0.5 ms wait drew the old level, 0.75 ms the new one); Unbound chooses at every render. The previous reference was a batch-mode capture with renders that close; windowed captures give the same records with or without the wait. Cross-fades are not drawn (deferred, see below) |

With it off, measured on Linux against the opt-in: texturepixels' three VolumeRGFloat rows per color space differ again (3 differences over tolerance 0, as before Q429), humanoid's bone.rotateThenSolve step 17 roll split differs again (muscles 41 and 43, within its bounded residual) while stream.bodyLocal step 17 matches, twod's spriteshape.render matches again (1 scenario differs instead of 2), and geometryframe2d, physics2ddynamics, physics2dmotion and query2dparity move by rounding with no failure; floatrounding, urp, particletriggerboundary and the other 50 of the 60 probes compared are unchanged; the other suite probes were not compared both ways (the sheriff baseline predates the rule, so a probe returning to its earlier values does not show as worse). Opted in: done for Unity 6000.0.71f1 script, package and precompiled plugin assemblies (tests/projects/floatrounding: Release 206/268 and Debug 215/268 values, 0 failures, the listed residuals below; the Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 Editors record identical values in both modes, two captures each). In the Editor a float on the evaluation stack is a double: chains, comparisons, conversions (`(int)`, `(double)`, `Math.Sqrt`) and values left on the stack across calls and joins keep it, and it is rounded to float where the IL stores it (locals, arguments, fields, array elements, indirect stores, kept boxes, closure/iterator/async fields, every call argument and return value, also of inlined, generic, interface and delegate calls, and `conv.r4`); `box` straight into `unbox.any` keeps it. Debug and Release differ only where the compiled IL keeps a local. Decision: a load-time IL rewrite, because it covers source-compiled and precompiled assemblies alike and no Roslyn option or CoreCLR knob reproduces the rule (Q402 controls). Unbound converts to double the float loads of each expression whose result double evaluation can change (an operation on another operation's result, or a result that is compared, converted or used other than by rounding it to float); one operation rounded straight away gives the same float and stays as it is; the runtime rounds stores and arguments ([ECMA-335](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-335/) III.1.1.1, III.1.6). Cost, macOS arm64 benchmark: a particle-style struct loop 1.5x, a scalar polynomial loop 1.2x (converting every float load would cost 3.3x by defeating inlining). Scope: `[BurstCompile]` methods and the `Execute` of `[BurstCompile]` job structs keep float arithmetic (the other methods of such types, and the methods Burst-compiled code calls, are converted; Burst in the Editor is unmeasured); a hot-reload edit is patched in place unless an edited method needs the conversions, which restarts the session (deltas are not converted); reflection on a converted method body shows the conversions and the calls to converted math (89 `il/` residuals). Unity's C# math in game code: row below. Open: other releases keep CoreCLR's float evaluation, unmeasured. The [C# specification 8.3.7](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/language-specification/types#837-floating-point-types) permits these wider intermediates. URP's `(int)(pixelWidth * renderScale)` (tests/projects/urp upscale_auto_fractional) is package code under the same rule and is re-checked by the Linux GPU suite; tests/projects/particletriggerboundary keeps its explicit double arithmetic, which equals the rule |

The engine's implementations of the methods Unity binds to native code compute in single precision with the Editor's algorithms and order: Quaternion.Slerp interpolates along the shorter arc with sines of the angle when the dot product is below 0.95 (unnormalized) and normalized linear interpolation above; Lerp is that normalized interpolation; AngleAxis converts degrees as angle / 360 doubled times PI and gives identity for an axis not longer than 1e-6; LookRotation builds an orthonormal frame and falls back to the shortest rotation from Z (identity for a forward not longer than 1e-5); FromToRotation uses Möller and Hughes' matrix (a half turn about an orthogonal axis for opposite directions); a rotation matrix becomes a quaternion by Shoemake's method, divided by its length; eulerAngles extracts Z, X, Y with gimbal lock beyond 0.499999; Vector3.Slerp and RotateTowards rotate the direction by an axis-angle matrix (straight interpolation within a dot product of 0.99999); Matrix4x4.inverse is Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting (zero for a zero pivot); rotation takes the matrix, its normalized columns or, for a mirroring or degenerate one, the rotation of its singular value decomposition (McAdams et al., five Jacobi sweeps), so a mirroring matrix keeps the reflection on its smallest-scale axis; lossyScale negates X by the 3x3 determinant's sign; Perspective takes the cotangent from a single-precision sine and cosine; Bounds Contains, SqrDistance and ClosestPoint compare against centre plus or minus extents (a point inside comes back unchanged). #### Rendering rules measured on one release

These answers of `Runtime/Compat.cs` give the behaviour measured on 6000.0.71f1 to every release
of the 6000.0 family (`Compat.RenderingMeasured`). Every other family takes the unmeasured answer
in the last column until a probe records it.

| Rule (`Compat.`) | Measured by (6000.0.71f1) | Other releases (unmeasured) |
|---|---|---|
| `RenderingMeasured`: world-space skinning retains its renderer's winding separately from the submitted model | samplerstates `RendererFaces.skinnedRenderer*`, `RendererFaces.commandSkinned*`, NVIDIA OpenGL Core/Vulkan | only the submitted model determinant is corrected |
| `RenderingMeasured`: Graphics and CommandBuffer blits execute shader passes without framebuffer GrabPass capture | textureformats `rt.padding.grab*`, renderer control; NVIDIA OpenGL Core | earlier all-pass selection including grabs |
| `DeviceTextureReadback`: device-specific ReadPixels conversion and signed RGB16 async clamp | textureformats `rt.readControl.*`, `rt.R16*`; NVIDIA OpenGL Core/Vulkan | framebuffer byte conversion, sampler padding and no RGB async clamp |
| `DeviceTextureReadback`: R16 async readback into a byte layout propagates red into green and blue and returns opaque alpha | textureformats `rt.unorm16Byte.*`, Linux OpenGL Core and Vulkan, Texture2D and RenderTexture with raw and half-float controls | missing components read as one |
| `ImmediateMeshKeepsWinding`: DrawMeshNow and CommandBuffer.DrawMesh preserve submitted winding | samplerstates `StencilFaces.*`, `RendererFaces.*` on OpenGL Core and Vulkan, NVIDIA only | determinant correction as for renderers |
| `MeshInstanceBatchLimits`: mesh-instancing IDs restart at 511/1023 transforms or 64 KiB of properties | cmdbuffers `graphics.meshinstances.*.batch.*` | sequential instance IDs, with a once-only warning |
| `GraphicsFenceFrames`: a CPU fence reports passed two frames after it ran | cmdbuffers `fence.*` | passed as soon as the GPU has passed it |
| `ZeroIndexedInstancesDrawOne`: `RenderPrimitivesIndexed` with 0 instances draws one | cmdbuffers `render.indexed.instances.zero` | draws none |
| `SkyAmbientWithoutLightColor`: the ambient projection of the sky draws it with `_LightColor0` zero (any sky material; only procedural skies with every disk mode were measured, so leaving out the colour rather than only the disk is a hypothesis until a sky tinted by `_LightColor0` is captured) | indirectspec, Q105 ambient controls | the sky projected as drawn, sun disk included |
| `SingleSubpassClearFillsOutputs`: a subpass with several color outputs of which exactly one clears clears them all to its color | urp `subpass_mrt`, `subpass_mrt_cleared`, `subpass_mrt_mixed` | each clearing output to its own color, the others kept |
| `RenderingMeasured`: texture readback conversion fills missing color components with 1, for byte, normalized, half and float sources | renderapi `volumeReadback.*`, 2D and 3D targets | R16/RG32 normalized sources fill with 1; other sources keep sampler padding |
| `ShaderKeywordsMeasured`: the built-in keyword registry and types | shaderkeywords | every name a global keyword, with a warning |
| `RenderingMeasured`: automatic render-target mips become visible when a subsequent draw prepares changed framebuffer attachments; public GenerateMips rejects automatic targets | renderapi `volumeMore.*`, `volumeAuto.*`, 2D and volume controls | automatic mips update after each render pass; GenerateMips is accepted |

A Don't Clear camera's intermediate that does not take the screen's depth starts with cleared
depth (measured for partial screen cameras and explicit full-rect HDR-to-byte targets,
cameraexplicitdepth). Explicit targets with image effects follow the same rule unmeasured.

Event attributes read in a spawn context (Get Attribute, Current) are the spawn context's own as the blocks before left them, in this update or the last, an event's attributes replacing them and one without giving the asset's initial values; a loop duration read so is the attribute the context holds when it plays, and one read shared by two contexts holds what either evaluated last (`event reads/*`). A read reaching past the spawn event's attributes makes the effect refused. Matrices built from rows, columns and axes and split into rows and columns, the inverse of any matrix (a camera's viewport point in the world; a matrix without an inverse gives zeros), a frame's position, angles (not made positive, of its rotation as it comes: a frame without a rotation of its own gives one not of unit length, which a script's `Quaternion.eulerAngles` would normalize) and scale (of its affine part), colour spaces (by the sixths of the hue circle; a hue outside the circle is not wrapped into it) and a texture's width and height (zero for none or one destroyed while set) and a buffer's count (kept for one released while set; a buffer released before it is set sets none) match the Editor (`operations/*`); known residual: a frame holding a NaN gives an x angle with the sign bit set where the Editor's has none (whether the rotation of such a matrix or the angle step differs is not isolated; the bits of `Matrix4x4.rotation` are not measured for such matrices) (the main camera's values: see "Visual Effect Graph: cameras"). Curves and gradients are sampled where expressions are evaluated (`sim/expressions*/inputs/*/c00`, `r00`; a curve's segments as cubics in the time from their first key, or where the curve ping-pongs as a sum of Hermite terms in the Editor's order, which both round differently from Unbound's `AnimationCurve.Evaluate`: `AnimationCurve.EvaluateCubic`, measured between the keys, where the curve loops after them, on its last key and where it ping-pongs before them; whether `AnimationCurve.Evaluate` called from a script rounds the same way in the Editor is not measured) and baked for the programs into the effect's texture (128 half-float texels a row, four curves to a row and a row to a gradient; a row whose values are larger than a half float holds is stored scaled with its scale; which row and channel a curve or gradient gets is a layout of Unbound's, since the programs find it only through the values baked with it), which the kernels and outputs sample as the package's code does (`draw-over life` with curves replaced from script, one of a single key and one whose keys span more than zero to one, `draw-hdr` with a fixed gradient stored scaled, and `draw-loop end` with the last sample of curves that loop after their last key only: images, exact); a curve another object replaces is baked again. Not measured: baked curves that ping-pong or loop before their first key only, a sampled curve that loops before its keys or ping-pongs after them, weighted and stepped keys in a sampled curve, null curves and gradients, gradients of one key or blended perceptually (tests/projects/vfx README). A curve or gradient baked among the expressions of a spawn event is not done: the graph is refused and says so. Output events (`events/*`). Documented (Scripting API 6000.0, [VisualEffect.outputEventReceived](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/ScriptReference/VFX.VisualEffect-outputEventReceived.html): Unity recycles the event attribute set it hands over; Visual Effect Graph 17.0 manual, [Output Event](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.visualeffectgraph@17.0/manual/Context-OutputEvent.html): the context sends an event whenever connected spawn contexts trigger it), with controls where the state diverged: every event of an effect hands over the same attribute set, holding the attributes of the event at hand (`same` rows, `events/kept attribute` a frame later). Observed in the captures: in each step, each spawn context feeding an output event that asked for at least one particle raises it once, in the order of its inputs (contexts of one name make one event: two inputs firing in one step raise it twice), the events of a step in the order of the systems and those of a frame in the order of its steps; the attribute set holds all the attributes of the spawn context that raised it (at their defaults where its blocks set none); events arrive after the scripts' `LateUpdate` and before the end of the frame; without a listener the step's events are dropped (a listener added later gets none of them); a listener's exception is logged and the step's next events are still handed over; a sole listener that removes itself leaves the step's next events each logging a call through nothing (`events once`); a culled effect raises none after its first update (which runs whole) and a paused one none until it plays. Not measured: a sole listener removed in a frame's earlier step while a later step of the frame raises events (Unbound drops that step's events without a log, as for any step without a listener), when, within the effects' update, the events are handed over (Unbound hands a step's events over at the end of the step, so a listener's `Stop`, `pause` or `SendEvent` takes effect from the effect's next step), a culled effect whose asset does not cull its simulation, events of prewarm steps or of `Simulate`, an asset replaced after events were handed over. A system that kills particles sleeps until it first spawns (`draw/over life`: its first count is asked for the frame after). A system whose kernel does not compile stops with an error and the effect's other systems keep running; without a renderer (a headless run) no kernel runs and the systems go on with the counts they keep themselves. Known residual of the probe: a coroutine waiting for the end of the frame resumes in the first Play frame in its capture and from the second in Unbound (the rule of tests/projects/eofstartup; what makes the two captures differ is not isolated). Noise on the CPU (value, Perlin and cellular over one, two and three coordinates with derivatives, and their curl; `VFX/VFXNoise.cs`) matches the Unity 6000.0.71f1 Editor bit for bit, in graphs and folded over constants (tests/projects/vfx `noise/*`, 2650 rows: lattice periods, huge, infinite and absent coordinates; in graphs with the octave count, roughness and lacunarity the operators' slots clamp, outside those ranges for the folded noise only, with counts of -1 to 5, which a graph reading them unclamped is taken to follow; more than eight octaves are not measured); the sign of a NaN is not compared, and the Voronoi noise stays refused on the CPU as the graph compiler refuses it. A matrix's axis (what collision shape blocks ask of an exposed frame) is evaluated, and a kernel that divides constants by zero in a branch it does not take (Position Shape over a cone of two equal constant radii) compiles: tests/projects/vfx `draw/collide`, `draw/cylinder`, images exact. |
| Visual Effect Graph: drawing | `VFX/VFXOutput.cs`, `VFX/VFXIndirectArgs.cs`, `VFX/VFXManager.cs` (the renderer), frame builder | W | partial, for Unity 6000.0.71f1 with URP 17 (tests/projects/vfx `draw-*` and tests/projects/vfxoutputs images and `draw/*` rows, pixel for pixel on the NVIDIA driver): unlit quad outputs that draw themselves (opaque or additive, without sorting) are drawn by the effect's renderer with the shader the graph compiled to, one indexed draw of the particles in the order the system keeps them: the particles spawned so far of a system that kills none, else its whole capacity (the vertex program leaves the dead out), all in one draw up to 16384 quads and in instances of 2048 beyond (`draw-many`), with the textures the output names. Triangle and octagon outputs are drawn the same ways (vfxoutputs `Triangle*`, `Octagon*`: directly, through the update kernel's list, 30000 at once): octagons as six triangles over their eight points, their odd corners pulled in by the crop factor in the vertex program, up to 8192 in one draw and in instances of 1024 beyond; triangles in one draw of 32-bit indices, as their vertex program reads no instance. Cube outputs (`Output Particle Cube`) are drawn the same ways (vfxoutputs `Cube*`: forty opaque cubes turned every way, directly and through the update kernel's list, and 10000 additive ones): twelve triangles over each cube's eight corners, every face facing out, up to 8192 in one draw and in instances of 1024 beyond (before, cube outputs were not drawn), all pixel for pixel. The texture lies on a face by the face number the program gives a triangle's corners, taken flat; on OpenGL Core, which takes flat values from a triangle's last vertex, Unbound's triangles lay it as the Editor's images on that device show it, on most faces across another axis than the face's own (`CubeTextured`, `CubeTexturedTurned`: six textured cubes, every face seen). The images do not tell a triangle's last corner from another that lays the texture alike, so cube outputs on a device taking flat values from the first vertex (Vulkan, Metal) are not measured and are refused there, saying so (all of them, also those the face number does not change). Not measured: sorted cubes, other cull modes, cubes edge-on to the camera, the depth passes of alpha-blended or alpha-clipped cubes, cube motion vectors and shadows. A forward decal output (deprecated, `Output Particle Forward Decal`) is not drawn and says so. Decal outputs of the render pipeline (`Output Particle URP Lit Decal`, boxes drawn as cubes are) are drawn by the pipeline's decal feature through their screen space pass, the technique the feature takes on OpenGL Core in a forward renderer (tests/projects/vfxlit `decal`: five turned decals of a mapped base colour on a lit wall, pixel for pixel); their DBuffer, GBuffer and emissive passes exclude OpenGL Core, which drops them, and on other devices (Vulkan, Metal), where the feature takes other techniques, they are refused and say so. Point and line outputs (`Output Particle Point`, `Output Particle Line` drawn as native lines) are drawn as triangles are, a point or a line from each particle's position to its target position per particle, in one draw of 32-bit indices, directly or through an indirect buffer (tests/projects/vfxlit `points`, `points listed`, `lines`, `lines listed`, sixty-four opaque ones each, pixel for pixel; before, they were not drawn); lines drawn as quads a pixel wide (the output's default) are quad outputs (`lines soft`, pixel for pixel). Not measured: sorted, blended and lit points and lines, and lines from a target offset. Single mesh outputs (`Output Single Mesh`, a system of its own) draw the effect's mesh value with the material made from the output's shader at the output's transform in the effect's space, one draw for each submesh its mask names, the shader's properties the output exposes set from the effect's values, a property the shader declares a colour set as a colour (gamma to linear in a linear project) (tests/projects/vfxlit `single mesh`: the pipeline's unlit and lit shaders, a turned and scaled transform, a mask of one submesh, pixel for pixel; the effect's renderer lists the outputs' materials and reports no system awake); before, such an effect was not simulated. The Editor's `ShaderUtil` property functions (count, names, descriptions, types, range limits, texture dimension, hidden and non-modifiable flags) answer as the shader's own (`ShaderUtilTests`), which the output's editor code reads. A single mesh output whose shader was not imported draws nothing and says so once. Not measured for single meshes: their order against the effect's particle outputs (drawn after them), shadows, the effect's bounds and culling with them (the effect's bounds are its particle systems'), two outputs of one shader (one material for both), vector and texture properties (properties of other types, such as a boolean, are not set), a mesh value changed while the effect plays. Not measured: decals through the deferred renderer, through a renderer without the decal feature, the order of overlapping decals (the output sorts by default), normal, mask and emissive maps, angle fade, decal layers. Unsorted quad outputs drawn through an indirect buffer are drawn from the list of particles to draw that the system's kernels make (vfxoutputs): the update kernel's (the output's indirect draw setting, the list emptied before each step), an output-update kernel's at each step (compute culling) or one made for each camera that sees the effect before that camera's draws (frustum culling; once for a camera and its view between two steps, however many of its draw lists take the effect); the draw's arguments are computed on the GPU from the list's count by the package's own kernels (`VFXFillIndirectArgs.compute`, `VFXCopyBuffer.compute`), entries any user can reserve (`VFXIndirectArgs`: a primitive's, a mesh's or a dispatch's), and the list skips dead particles and reaches past 16384 quads in instances. Frustum culling is documented to cull the particles outside the camera's frustum ([Visual Effect Graph 17.0, Shared Output Settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.visualeffectgraph@17.0/manual/Context-OutputSharedSettings.html)); URP 17 declares the culling kernel's frustum planes and never sets them (read off the pipeline's sources), and Unbound gives the kernel none, so it culls nothing (what the Editor's kernel reads is not measured: no image can tell, as a particle outside the view is not seen either way). The order of an unsorted list is documented as not deterministic (same page, Sort), so no control shows it: alpha-blended outputs with sorting off are drawn, not measured. In the Editor (OpenGL Core, NVIDIA) the per-camera lists of systems of 4096 particles and more were drawn incompletely and differently from capture to capture (20000 particles: 5 and 32 drawn in two captures, all in two others; 16384: a few drawn elsewhere, the same way in six shots); Unbound draws every particle the kernel keeps, and the per-camera controls have at most 64 particles, where every capture agreed (tests/projects/vfxoutputs README). A system that kills particles asks for its alive count only in a frame it updated (`away`). Sorted outputs (alpha-blended outputs sort by default) draw their list sorted by the package's own kernels (`Sort.compute`: decreasing keys, equal keys by increasing particle index, one pass up to 4096 particles, chunks merged beyond: `SortKeyedMany`, 20000 sorted at each step; a large list sorted for each camera is not shot, as the Editor's per-camera lists of large systems are not repeatable) after the kernel that writes the keys, at each step or for each camera, by distance, camera depth, age (youngest in front), a custom key, each reversible (vfxoutputs `Sort*`, two cameras each); an effect's outputs are drawn by their priority (`sortPriority`, the asset's [Output Render Order](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.visualeffectgraph@17.0/manual/VisualEffectGraphAsset.html): "Unity draws items at the top of the list first"), the lowest first, equal ones in their systems' order, then each system's (`Priority`, `PriorityTies`); effects over each other are drawn from the farther, whatever the order they were made in (`Effects`), effects at one distance are not measured. The generated shaders needed two things of the shader pipeline (three with the package's indirect-argument kernel, which writes a `RWBuffer<uint>`: typed buffers of one 32-bit scalar are translated as structured buffers of it; other typed buffers still fail to translate, loudly): names holding the separator of a shader selection (`…/Output Particle|Unlit Quad`), and constants that are not numbers (the vertex programs put `asfloat(~0u)` in the clip position of a particle they do not draw), which a function now makes at run time where it stores, returns, passes, selects, merges or computes with one (a constant used another way, such as one of a whole constant vector or array, still fails to compile, and says so; the module of a program with such constants is also compacted earlier than others, which on Vulkan and Metal is not measured where a texture is read only by an unused statement). Motion vectors: an opaque quad output that writes them is drawn into the camera's motion vectors (URP Motion Blur, Camera and Objects) from its particles' clip positions of this frame and the one before, kept in the effect's rings of temporary buffers per camera (tests/projects/vfxoutputs `MovingVectors` and its control without them, `MovingPlain`, frames 9 and 10, pixel for pixel: one still camera, an effect at rest, particles three frames old), and so are quads lit by the render pipeline and unlit meshes (tests/projects/vfxlit `moving lit`, `moving meshes`, pixel for pixel but one pixel a level apart). Not measured: several cameras on one effect, a moving camera (URP sets the view-projection the kernel reads in its own motion vectors pass, after the effects' camera commands), an effect whose transform moves, particles born in the frame drawn, an effect culled for some frames and seen again, an effect's first frame (new buffers are not cleared), a camera rendered twice in a frame, projection jitter and XR (one view), and how long a camera's buffers are kept unused (Unbound's own: `VisualEffect.UnusedCameraFrames`). Outputs that share their sort (the compiler's global sort: a keys kernel over the system's list, sorted through the system's two sort buffers back into that list), for each camera by distance and at each step by age, beside an output of the system that sorts its own list (tests/projects/vfxoutputs `GlobalDistance`, `GlobalMixed`, `GlobalYoungest`, two cameras, pixel for pixel); a keys kernel that does not compile leaves the system simulating and its sharing outputs drawing nothing, as the Editor does with the package's kernel for a custom key read from the graph's values (`GlobalKeyed`). Not measured: a global sort longer than one sort pass (merged through the scratch list), a custom key that compiles, and reversed sorts. Open: a strip system's global sort (refused), lit outputs (the pipeline's lighting and probes per draw), motion vectors of lit mesh, transparent, strip, Shader Graph and cube outputs and of particles that turn or change size between frames, motion vectors of points and lines, shadows cast by an effect, and the `VFXManager` camera hooks (`PrepareCamera`, `ProcessCameraCommand`, camera buffers). Soft particles are drawn as the Visual Effect Graph: cameras row says (measured with outputs drawn directly; an indirect output's are drawn the same way, not measured). An output that is not drawn says so once for its asset with the reason (lit, soft particles and passes other than the measured ones are read off the shader the graph compiled to, at import: the pass list admits only what is measured, the two defines exclude what URP 17 is known to add, so another input a later package adds to the unlit forward pass would have to be added here), its system is simulated all the same, and `unbound doctor` lists the project's effects. An effect whose asset asks for shadows is drawn without and says so; a script that turns shadow casting on for an effect's renderer itself is not measured. Not measured: the built-in pipeline (the package draws under a scriptable pipeline only), the 2D renderer, a depth prepass of opaque outputs, quads turned to face a camera that does not look straight at them (and quads seen at an angle, whose crossings the Editor's own graphs decide differently from each other), other devices than OpenGL Core in the Editor (the images' zero limits hold on the one machine both ran on), and how a system that sleeps is drawn (Unbound draws none of its particles: they are all dead). Generated shaders of one name (graphs of one file name in different folders, outputs of one system named alike) each draw with their own source: an importer's generated ShaderLab is known to the renderer by its name joined with its source's hash (`Shader.m_SourceKey`; Shader.name stays the ShaderLab name), which also keeps a graph's earlier versions left in LibraryUnbound/GeneratedShaders from being drawn (tests/projects/vfxoutputs `TwinA`, `TwinB`, `AlikeOutputs`, pixel for pixel). A `Fallback`, `UsePass` or lookup by a generated shader's plain name finds the most recently written generated file of that name unless a project or package shader has it (which of several Unity takes is not specified); generated files from before the keys are passed over. Project and package `.shader` files of one name each draw their own source too (see the Q696 row). |

Mesh outputs also draw through an indirect buffer: one indexed indirect draw of each submesh the mask names, its arguments computed from the list's count by the package's arguments kernel with the submesh's index count, first index and base vertex, described anew when the mesh changes; pixel for pixel for unlit and lit wedges blended over what is behind them, which sort by default (`mesh sorted`, `mesh lit sorted`), opaque ones from the update's unsorted list (`mesh listed`), and a mesh of one submesh set in place of one of two while the effect plays (`mesh sorted` frame 10). A quad output drawn by a Shader Graph of the older (deprecated) Visual Effect target is drawn (`graph legacy`), and so is a mesh output whose graph samples a sampling node's default texture, a texture slot nothing feeds (`graph legacy mesh`; before, its shader did not compile: see the row on textures read from the struct a call returns), and lit quads and meshes through the 2D renderer are as the Editor draws them (`lit 2d`: nothing; `mesh 2d`). Residuals: the same quads baked in the emitter's frame (no BakePosition/BakeRotationAndScale) from a rotated emitter scaled (1.5, 0.5, 2): the particle moving along the emitter's y turns by another angle (`freemove/transform_freeform/*/front/positions`, `freeform-stretching`, 3 keys; Q278: its stretch lies along the camera's up in that frame, where Unbound's angle, taken from the cosine to the camera's up times the y scale, chooses its side by the sign of a near-zero component along the camera's right and comes out mirrored about the quad's long axis, while the Editor's quad does not depend on that sign; the rest of the freeform bakes, which this angle fits, leave no other key to tell how the Editor builds the turned quad, so the rule stays open); side-view normals within 1e-3 (`stretched-normals`); texels past the data hold the Editor's scratch memory (`bake-scratch-memory`). First visibility (`firstvis/*`): culling bounds are the particles' (the emitter point without one); frames with zero frame time keep the last bounds (a seen system stays seen after an Emit or Play, one whose particles are all out of view stays unseen with its emitter in view); a system that never had bounds (played or emitted by script, never updated while time moved, never rendered) has nothing to draw after a zero-time update (invisible at once) until time moves (at any simulation speed) or a Simulate; Play On Awake and a render before any update give bounds; a playback's two grace updates are updates that move time; Play restarts a playing system that is not emitting (emission module off), keeping its particles. Sub-emitters update while their parent updates or their own renderer is seen, whatever their own culling mode (`subcull/*`); a Birth child's start of play and first births under a played parent now match (see the sub-emitters row). LimitVelocity's dampen defaults to 0 (measured). `safeCollisionEventSize` and force-field vector fields done (tests/projects/particlecollision): the safe size counts the system's events of the update; the velocity relaxes toward the nearest texel of the field's Texture3D (over its range, turned with the field) times vectorFieldSpeed by vectorFieldAttraction × External Forces multiplier × 30 × dt, unclamped, only with a positive attraction and not in the system's first step, with or without particles (a particle emitted later is moved in its first step; a fresh system in a field already used is not); the texels are read again when the texture changes (updateCount). Applied for a Box field without scale, with constant speed and attraction and without drag or rotation; other shapes, scaled fields, curves and those combinations are reported as unsupported (unmeasured). | Clips that animate different parts: legacy Animation blending and fades; Animator blend trees, transition timing; animated bools | `Animation/Animation.cs`, `AnimationPose.cs` (`WriteLegacy`), `AnimatorPlayer.cs` (`SampleState`, `Step`), `Binding.cs` (`AnimatedBool`) | S | done for generic rigs, and for humanoid clips that animate only some muscles, on Unity 6000.0.71f1 (tests/projects/animpartial, 1192 records: 462 from two identical windowed GPU Editor captures on Linux, 730 from identical pairs of batchmode captures of the macOS Editor). Legacy Animation: each channel is shared among the states that animate it (states at a weight of 1e-4 or less add nothing), higher layers first, a layer's sum counting as at most 1 and leaving the rest times (1 − sum) to the layers below, normalized to full weight, so a lone state at half weight plays in full and what no state animates is not written; a clip's rotation curves blend as they evaluate (unnormalized) and the sum is normalized; additive states add their difference from their clip's first keys, by their weight up to 1, to the result or to the current value (where it accumulates), on a Transform's position, rotation (the difference turned towards the identity) and scale only. Fades run at a constant speed from the update after a state is enabled and end when the weight passes its target; a state that stops in an update is sampled once more at its last time with a weight of 1.001e-4; Play stops the others of the layer at weight 0, Stop keeps the weight; a clip played once (or by default) fades out over the length of the CrossFade or Blend that started it before its end (Play: stops a step after it, weight 0); disabling the component keeps its states, whose time catches up when it is enabled again; deactivating the GameObject stops them. Animator: a blend tree child's share of a channel it has no curve for takes the default value with write defaults and the current value without; the state a Play/CrossFade request enters and the state a transition completes into check their transitions from the next update (the default state in the first). Bools (GameObject activity, Behaviour and Renderer enabled, bool fields) are true beyond 0.001 from 0; ints round to the nearest. The 6000.0 Scripting API documents only the fade ([Animation.Blend](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.0/script-reference/unityengine/animation/blend): "towards targetWeight over the next time seconds", other animations not affected); the shares, normalization and fade timing above are this capture's observations. From the macOS Editor's captures (records that do not depend on the OS; the captures' other records equal the Linux reference's): an Any State transition whose condition holds in the update a Play request enters a state is skipped there with the state's own and starts in the next update (`any.request`, against `any.plain` and `any.first`); a Once clip played backwards from its end (speed -1) plays to time 0 and stops there as at its end (`legacy.once.reverse`, also cross-faded in); every enabled legacy state fires the events its time passes, whatever its weight (`legacy.events.zero`: weight 0), also in the update its fade stops it (`legacy.events.fade`; before this Unbound skipped them), and Stop fires none; an update that does not move a state's time fires none of its events: its first after Play, CrossFade or Blend, which samples its start, and those at speed 0; an event at its start fires in the first update that moves its time (`legacy.events.start.*`, at weights 1, 0 and fading in, and at speed 0 for three updates; before this Unbound fired it in the first); humanoid clips that animate only some muscles (`human.*` on the humanoid probe's HumanA: alone, in transitions from one such clip to another and from a whole clip, in 1D trees, on override layers of weight 1 and 0.6 and additive layers of weight 0.6, with and without a humanoid mask, write defaults on and off; also tests/projects/humanoid body.partialOverride, bodyGraph.layerPartial): the muscles a clip lacks play at rest with its weight wherever it plays, matched as implemented. Also measured with the macOS Editor (Q511): a time set on a legacy state (time, normalizedTime, Rewind of one state or of all; measured with one state playing) makes the next update that moves its time fire the events from that time on, one at that very time too, while it plays (`legacy.events.timeset`, `legacy.events.normalizedtimeset`, `legacy.events.rewind`, `legacy.events.rewindall`; normalizedTime a fraction of the length, `legacy.normalizedtime.scaled`), in the update Play starts it and while it is held at speed 0 (`legacy.events.start.timeset`, `.speed0.timeset`; before this Unbound skipped an event at the time set on a playing state); Blend and CrossFade of a state Stop left at its weight and Play of a once clip during the fade out a CrossFade gave it before its end play as implemented (`legacy.stop.blend`, `legacy.stop.crossfade`, `legacy.once.fade.play`); SpriteRenderer flipX/flipY and CanvasGroup interactable, blocksRaycasts and ignoreParentGroups are true beyond 0.001 from 0 like the other bools and CanvasGroup alpha follows its curve, Animator and legacy alike (`flags.*`, `legacy.flags.*`). Unmeasured (implemented by the same rules): a once clip's fade out starting between updates (measured only where it starts a whole update before one: its first update moves the weight by the time past its start and then by the update's time), Any State transitions in the update a transition enters a state and interruptions in the update a request or a transition enters one (skipped with the state's own), a weight set, Rewind or a time set during a once clip's fade out before its end (a weight set ends it, and it starts again from the time past its start at the next update; Rewind and a time set leave it running), states enabled while the component is disabled, where an event handler sees the pose of the update that fires it (Unbound writes the pose first), additive Euler curves, and humanoid clips without muscle curves (body curves alone) on layers |

A Polygon-mode sprite's mesh is always Tight (mesh type and the 32-pixel minimum do not apply), and its default physics shape is one path through the vertices of its mesh's boundary edges, in the order of an edge hash table whose shape reproduces every Polygon control: separate islands and holes follow each other in that one path; a zero-area outline renders the quad and takes its boundary (a texture without traceable alpha or a rect outside the texture take the same quad, unmeasured). Thirteen Polygon controls (concave with an off-centre pivot, islands, hole, 60 vertices, two loops of 160 edges that pin that table's shape, custom and disabled shapes, Full Rect, under 32 pixels, no outline, zero-area outline). Runtime `Sprite.Create` traces the texture as the importer does (tests/projects/spriteoutlines, 12,059 values, zero differences; two independent macOS Editor captures identical, equal to the earlier Linux Editor reference in its 5,332 values): the Tight mesh and texture rect (a rect under 32 pixels on a side stays a quad; extrude 0 and 1 trace alike), and with `generateFallbackPhysicsShape` the traced physics shape; readable and unreadable imported textures alike, and the texels the CPU holds when a script wrote them: a new texture before and after `Apply`, one `Apply(false, true)` made non-readable, an imported readable texture rewritten by `SetPixels32` (applied or not). Only the rect's texels are handed to the trace; an imported texture nothing rewrote is traced from its import (floating-point textures unmeasured: an imported one is not traced, one a script made is traced from its 8-bit reading). A PolygonCollider2D added in Play mode to a sprite's object takes the sprite's physics shape, else the outline a generated physics shape would have (also for Full Rect sprites; holes give extra paths); a TilemapCollider2D's sprite tiles take the same outline (convex outlines measured; the decomposition of an outline with holes into tile shapes is not part of the probe). `UnityEditor.Sprites.SpriteUtility.GenerateOutline` traces a texture rect with its detail, alpha tolerance and hole detection, in pixels from the rect's centre, and `Sprite.OverridePhysicsShape` takes paths in rect space to units from the pivot (a null path throws `ArgumentNullException` and one under 3 points `ArgumentException`, before any path is set; no paths clear the shape; `GenerateOutline` of no texture throws `ArgumentNullException`); the SVG importer's generated physics shape uses both (tests/projects/svgsprites). `SpriteUtility.GenerateOutlineFromSprite` (the PSD and Aseprite importers' generated physics shapes) traces the sprite's rect with its arguments in units from its pivot (the generated physics shape with the importers' arguments); a Polygon-mode sprite's is its mesh's boundary, whatever the arguments; no sprite throws `ArgumentNullException`. Colliders added to an object with a renderer fit its local bounds (through the renderer's matrix into the object's space, so flips and Sliced or Tiled sizes count): a Circle takes the larger half extent, a Capsule the bounds, an Edge a level line across them (the default edge for bounds narrower than about 1.005e-4: 1.004e-4 measured default, 1.006e-4 level, with the centre at 0.5 only; ends that are not finite at the origin), a Polygon the sprite's outline unflipped, else a pentagon of the larger half extent around their centre; a Box takes a sprite renderer's sprite bounds in Simple drawing, flipped, whatever the draw mode (set local bounds instead when there are some; no sprite: the smallest size); an offset whose centre is not finite is zero; without a renderer or with empty bounds the defaults stay. A sprite renderer's local bounds mirror through the pivot when flipped. `PolygonCollider2D.CreatePrimitive` and the default pentagon have radius `scale` (half that before); Box and Capsule sizes and Circle radii keep at least 0.0001 per component, radii at most 1e6. Not measured: a renderer whose object differs from the collider's, the Box's tiling state for Tiled sprites (`autoTiling` stays as set). |

Q64/Q221/Q287: instance multipliers on CPU-expanded mesh instances: done for Unity 6000.0.71f1 on OpenGL Core (tests/projects/cmdbuffers `device.multiplier.mesh.*`, `placed.*`, `camera.*`; NVIDIA only). The Editor multiplies a mesh-instancing call's GPU instance count (the Scripting API: "multiply the instance count of every draw call"), through command buffers and a camera's queued `Graphics.RenderMeshInstanced` and `DrawMeshInstanced`; the added IDs n to n·m − 1 have `unity_InstanceID` equal to the raw ID and read the instance data past the call's elements. Unbound adds them after the call's last instance with zero matrices and instanced properties, which is what the Editor reads where no earlier draw wrote there, and with the last instance's winding (Unbound's choice). Measured, not reproduced: where earlier instanced draws wrote more elements, the Editor's added instances read those (data left in its instance buffer, `device.multiplier.stale.colors.2`, kept as a visible difference); Unbound warns once. The ID-placed color cases (`placed.colors.*`, `camera.colors.*`) record only the call's own instances' columns on every device since Q586: a call of six clear-colored instances before them did not define what the added instances read once earlier sections were added (two captures read colors of earlier sections). Unmeasured: other per-instance built-ins of the added instances (LOD fade, probes, lightmap scale/offset keep the draw's values), standalone instancing whose multiplied IDs pass a native batch (warned, not added), stereo instancing keywords (XR deferred).


Q274: compute shaders keep predefined sampler states on the measured 6000.0.71f1 OpenGL Core
device (`tests/projects/renderapi` `computeSamplers.*`). Texture-named samplers continue to use
the texture's filter and wrap settings, including `volumeCompute.*.point`; the graphics-program
inline sampler observation does not apply to compute kernels. The URP `upscale_stp` comparison
is retained by `tests/projects/renderapi/stp.py`.

Q221 shader-declarations replies preserve a reason and retry flag for opaque per-pass variant choices, including serialized built-ins and generated surface passes. A known empty choice list remains distinct from an unreadable one; managed caching retries transient per-pass inputs and accepts replies from older hosts. Provider and managed metadata tests cover these transport guarantees.
